Description

X39CrMo17-1 Flat Bars / EN 1.4122 Flat Bars

X39CrMo17-1 Flat Bars also known as EN 1.4122, is a heat-treatable stainless steel containing chromium and molybdenum, providing an excellent combination of wear resistance, corrosion resistance, and high mechanical strength. It is widely used for components exposed to abrasion, moisture, and moderate corrosive environments.

1.4122 (X39CrMo17-1) is a martensitic stainless steel characterised by good mechanical properties and the possibility of specific heat treatment (hardening). Due to its chromium content of 17%, the material has good corrosion resistance in slightly aggressive media with a low chlorine content. The material is easy to polish (high-gloss polishing is possible) and is magnetisable/magnetic. The material has a tensile strength of 750 to 950 N/mm², a hardness of ≤ 280 (in condition +A). The material is not very suitable for welding and is also only moderately forgeable. Cold forming and cold heading are not intended for this material and it is rarely used for machining / machining.

X39CrMo17-1 / 1.4122 is a martensitic steel with high wear resistance and good corrosion resistance in environments with low chloride content. The corrosion resistance can be further improved by surface polishing.

The stainless steel X39CrMo17-1 (1.4122) is often used to make cutting tools such as knives, but it is also used in mechanical engineering or in polymer processing.
